functional.text: get(key) returns the value (and marks it most recently used) or a miss; put(key, value) inserts or updates.
Capacity is fixed at construction (e.g. 10,000 entries).
When full, put evicts the least recently used entry; the eviction rule is pluggable (LFU, TTL later).
Hit/miss statistics and an optional on-evict callback.

non_functional.text: Thread-safe under dozens of concurrent threads (~90% reads) without one global bottleneck.

assumptions.text: Keys are hashable; values are opaque; size counted in entries, not bytes.

out_of_scope.text: Distribution across machines, persistence, size in bytes.

api.notes: Moves the entry to most recent; counts a hit or a miss.
Updates in place or inserts; evicts the policy's victim when full and fires on_evict.

data.name: index
data.why: O(1) lookup of the node for a key.

data.name: recency list
data.fields: doubly linked list of Node(key, value, prev, next) with sentinel head/tail

data.name: Segment
data.fields: LRUCache + its own lock; segment = hash(key) % N

deep_dives.title: Constant-time structures

options.name: hash map + doubly linked list
options.cons: two structures to keep in sync

deep_dives.choice: hash map key → node + doubly linked list ordered by recency
deep_dives.why: get = lookup + move to head; put = insert at head and pop the tail when full; every step is O(1). The node stores its key so eviction can delete it from the map.

deep_dives.title: Thread safety

options.name: one global mutex
options.cons: every call serialises; 30 threads queue up

options.name: read-write lock
options.cons: useless here: get moves the node, so it is a write

deep_dives.choice: SegmentedCache: N segments by hash(key) % N, each an LRUCache with its own mutex; a single-lock ThreadSafeCache decorator for small caches
deep_dives.why: Because even reads reorder the list, a read-write lock buys nothing; splitting the key space removes the single hot lock, and per-segment LRU is an acceptable approximation. Callbacks run outside the lock so user code cannot deadlock the cache.

wrapup.bottlenecks: A single lock around the list; removed by segmenting. Very hot single keys still serialise on their segment.
wrapup.failures: An on_evict callback that throws or blocks: run callbacks after releasing the lock and swallow/log their errors.
wrapup.monitoring: Hit ratio, eviction rate, lock wait time per segment.
wrapup.scale: New rules (LFU, TTL) are new EvictionPolicy implementations; stats and callbacks are decorators/listeners around any Cache; more threads → more segments. Size-by-bytes would make capacity a weigher function.
wrapup.future: Lock-free reads with buffered recency updates (sample and apply in batches), a distributed tier behind the same Cache interface.
